facts.raw_span: intermittent fever
unintentional weight loss
progressive lip swelling with painful ulcerations
his CD4 count rising from 94 to 160 cells/mm3
undetectable HIV viral load
undetectable hepatitis C viral load
no hepatosplenomegaly
a polymerase‐chain‐reaction assay for herpes simplex virus from an ulcer base was negative
Complement C1 esterase inhibitor levels were within normal limits
Gram stain, acid‐fast stain, and mucicarmine stain of lesion samples were negative
Fungal blood cultures and both urine and serum Histoplasma antigen tests were negative
lips were markedly edematous, with multiple superficial ulcers having heaped‐up margins

concepts.why: The patient's lip swelling and ulcerations, combined with normal Complement C1 esterase inhibitor levels, suggest acquired angioedema.
The patient's lip swelling and ulcerations, with heaped-up margins, are consistent with cheilitis glandularis.
The patient's intermittent fever, unintentional weight loss, and lip swelling could be indicative of mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome.
The patient's lip ulcerations, with heaped-up margins, could be consistent with eosinophilic ulcer of the lip.
The patient's lip swelling and ulcerations, combined with the absence of other systemic symptoms, could suggest Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome.
The patient's lip lesions developed approximately two months after the CD4 count began to improve, suggesting an immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome.

rationales.F03: The presence of progressive lip swelling with painful ulcerations is more typical of Cheilitis glandularis, Eosinophilic ulcer of the lip, and Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome.
rationales.F04: The rising CD4 count suggests an improvement in the patient's immune status, which could be related to Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome (IRIS).
rationales.F05: The undetectable HIV viral load could be related to IRIS, as it indicates a strong immune response.
rationales.F09: Normal Complement C1 esterase inhibitor levels make Acquired angioedema less likely.
rationales.F12: The presence of markedly edematous lips with multiple superficial ulcers having heaped-up margins is more typical of Cheilitis glandularis, Eosinophilic ulcer of the lip, and Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms developed after his CD4 count began to improve and he had an undetectable HIV viral load, which supports the diagnosis of IRIS, an inflammatory condition that can occur in response to immune recovery.
